newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: SYNOPOSIS OF CZECH GOVT ECONOMIC MEASURES - PART II.
newsitem.headline: SYNOPOSIS OF CZECH GOVT ECONOMIC MEASURES - PART II.

text.p: The following is a continuation of an unofficial synopsis of the Czech government's package of economic measures released on Wednesday:
ON TRANSPARENCY AND STANDARDISATION OF CAPITAL AND FINANCIAL MARKETS:

*We must establish an independent securities commission. The task of this commission will be supervision of the capital markets. For this, a new law will be prepared, by May 13, by the Ministry of Finance for discussion by the goverment.

*To analyse the situation in the financial sector with the aim of making better relations between banks, investment funds and companies and to eliminate all conflicts of interests. This analysis should help limit the connections between banks, investment funds and companies. The Finance Ministry and central bank, together with Justice Ministry, should prepare within three months new proposals.
*Enforce very quickly any amendments to the law, which will lower tax deductable items and provisions for banks.

*Prepare an amendement to the law on investment funds and companies which will forbid funds and managers and employees of these investment companies from including relatives from owning shares in the investment and mutual funds administered by them or to own shares in firms which are in the funds' portfolio.

*Prepare an amendment to the law on investment funds and investment companies, which will forbid them from performing transactions with the property of the funds through related companies which create a conflict of interest.
*The above two amendments will be prepared within a month.
*Take measures to make prices on securities market more transparent. This will be done by the Finance Ministry together with Prague bourse and other bourses within three months.
*Clearly separate banks' loan operations from their portfolio management functions. At the same time to ban bank officials from being members of supervisory boards of firms.
*The Finance Ministry will immediately check the performance of banks as custodions. Shortfalls may be punished by the withdrawal of banking licences.
*Create stricter reporting requirements and strengthen capital sufficiency of subjects on the capital markets.
ON IMPROVEMENT OF CONDITIONS FOR PRIVATE BUSINESS AND EXPORT, THE PROTECTION OF THE DOMESTIC MARKET:
*Increase the possibility for write-offs of old uncollectable receivables to 20 percent from 10 percent.

*In making decisions on public orders, domestic supliers and producers will be preferred to foreign subjects. Producers will also be preferred to intermediaries. A minimum level of domestic participation should be set in tender conditions.
*Quickly change and strengthen the bankruptcy law.
*To increase the efficieny of regulation of natural monopolies including price issues.
*Enhance activities of the Czech Export Bank (CEB) and the export insurance company EGAP.
*Prepare an export support programme through EGAP, CEB and Konsolidacni Banka.
*Prepare minimal import prices in the agricultural sector in order to fight subsidised imports
*Impose acceptable seasonal import quotas on agricultural commodities and foodstuffs.
ON PUBLIC FINANCES:
*Regulate municipal indebtedness.
*Reduce the number of hospital beds and eliminate indebtedness of health care facilities.
*Introduce central budgetary financing and administration of state hospitals.
*Prepare rules for efficiency in spending in the public sector generally.
*Prepare a new law on the execution of ownership rights in remaining state holdings.
ON MEASURES AGAINST ECONOMIC AND FINANCIAL CRIME:
*Set up a team formed from different state organs to fight criminality in the markets.
*Propose a law to create a special state organ to operate alongside the supreme state prosecution office to fight criminality in the banking sector.
*Immediately to investigate reasons for delays in prosecution of economic crime and delays in bankruptcies.
*New sections are to be added to the criminal code to deal with economic crime.
-- Prague Newsroom, 420-2-2423-0003
